newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WINDY FORECAST DELIGHT OPEN ORGANISERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WINDY FORECAST DELIGHT OPEN ORGANISERS.

text.p: Ernie Els and Greg Norman played Royal Troon in a stiff breeze on Sunday and then learned the forecast was for more of the same when the British Open begins on Thursday.
Michael Bonallack, secretary of the Royal and Ancient Golf Club tournament organisers, said the forecast was exactly what they wanted.

After three practice days of showers and reasonably calm conditions, the wind is expected to pick up on Thursday morning and develop into a testing breeze in the afternoon. Friday's forecast is similar.

U.S. Open champion Els said he and Norman played the front nine with the strongest wind of the day when it was behind them. Then it died as they played the back. "Just what you want it to do," he said.
"The back nine is still tough and will play very long but the golf course is in excellent shape," Els said.
Greg Turner of New Zealand played earlier and caught the back nine, one of the toughest finishing stretches on the Open rota, with the stiffest wind of the day in his face..
"It's five or six shots tougher in that wind," Turner said. "I could not get up (to the green) at 13 or 15 and then the wind died a bit.
"The 17th would have been driver or a three-wood in that wind," he added.
The 13th and 15th are par fours of 465 and 457 yards respectively. The 17th is a par three of 223 yards.
